issues.legal_issue: A difference between the fair market value of a transferred asset and its declared consideration, without understatement of the consideration actually received, does not permit the fair market value to be substituted as the consideration for computing capital gains.
material_facts: The asset was sold for the same price for which it had been purchased.
The revenue authorities found that the sale was an honest and bona fide transaction and that the consideration received was correctly disclosed.
The proposed assessment relied on the fair market value being substantially higher than the declared sale price.
issues.conclusion: The statutory fair-market-value substitution could be used only where the consideration had been understated; it did not apply to an honest transaction in which the consideration received was correctly disclosed.
issues.legal_principle: The provision must be construed in light of its purpose and statutory context, rather than by a literal reading that produces absurd or unjust results. The Court read a requirement of understatement into the provision, relying on its purpose of reaching concealed consideration, its marginal note and placement, and contemporaneous administrative circulars. The mover’s speech may be used to identify the mischief and purpose of legislation. Circulars issued under section 119 bind the revenue authorities even if they depart from the correct statutory interpretation. Relevant authorities include Luke v. Revenue Commissioner, Heydon’s Case, In re May Fair Property Company, Eastman Photographic Material Company v. Comptroller-General of Patents, Bushel v. Hammond, Bengal Immunity Company Ltd. v. State of Bihar, Navnitlal C. Jhaveri v. R.K. Sen, and Ellerman Lines Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

rule.if: capital_gains_transfer_case and market_value_gap_exceeds_tolerance and consideration_correctly_disclosed and bona_fide_transaction

predicates.capital_gains_transfer_case: The proceeding concerns the computation of capital gains on a transfer of a capital asset.
predicates.market_value_gap_exceeds_tolerance: The asset’s fair market value exceeds the consideration declared for the transfer by more than the permitted margin.
predicates.consideration_correctly_disclosed: The transferor disclosed the full consideration actually received for the transfer.
predicates.bona_fide_transaction: The transfer was an honest transaction without concealment or suppression of consideration.

issues.definition: When a capital-gains transfer has a qualifying market-value gap but the transfer was bona fide and the consideration received was correctly disclosed, fair market value cannot be substituted for that consideration.

issues.legal_issue: The revenue bears the burden of proving understatement of consideration independently of proving a sufficient difference between fair market value and declared consideration.
material_facts: The revenue sought to substitute the asset’s fair market value for the declared consideration.
The revenue relied on the difference between fair market value and declared consideration, but the transaction was found to be bona fide and the consideration received correctly disclosed.
issues.conclusion: The revenue must establish both the required market-value difference and that the transferor received more than was declared; proof of the market-value difference alone does not establish understatement.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of establishing the conditions of taxability rests on the revenue. Under the provision considered, the qualifying difference in values is a safeguard against hardship in marginal valuation cases, not evidence that consideration was understated. Under section 52(2), once understatement is proved, the fair market value may serve as a statutory measure of the consideration actually received; it does not create a fictional receipt. This must be read with section 48, which computes capital gains from consideration received or accruing. The Court also relied on the principle that placing on the taxpayer the burden of proving the negative—that no additional consideration was received—would impose an almost impossible burden.

predicates.capital_gains_transfer_case: The proceeding concerns the computation of capital gains on a transfer of a capital asset.
predicates.revenue_seeks_market_value_substitution: The revenue seeks to use fair market value in place of the consideration declared for a transfer.

issues.definition: When the revenue seeks market-value substitution in a capital-gains transfer case, it must prove that the consideration received was understated.

issues.legal_issue: Reassessment for escaped income cannot be sustained when the transfer was bona fide, the consideration was correctly disclosed, and no income escaped assessment under the applicable capital-gains rule.
material_facts: The original assessment included no capital gains from the transfer because the asset was sold for its purchase price.
The revenue later sought to reopen the assessment and tax the difference between fair market value and declared consideration.
The revenue authorities found that the transaction was bona fide and the consideration received was correctly disclosed.
issues.conclusion: The reassessment notice had no jurisdictional basis because the applicable capital-gains provision did not apply and there was no reason to believe that income had escaped assessment; the reassessment order was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 148 could not support reopening without a basis to believe that income had escaped assessment. Because section 52(2) applied only where consideration was understated, and the consideration here was correctly disclosed in a bona fide transaction, the proposed fair-market-value difference was not taxable as capital gains. Sections 45 and 48 govern the charge and computation of capital gains, and the computation begins with consideration received or accruing.

rule.if: reassessment_challenge and bona_fide_transaction and consideration_correctly_disclosed and no_escaped_capital_gains_income

predicates.reassessment_challenge: The proceeding challenges a reassessment initiated on the ground that income escaped assessment.
predicates.bona_fide_transaction: The transfer was an honest transaction without concealment or suppression of consideration.
predicates.consideration_correctly_disclosed: The transferor disclosed the full consideration actually received for the transfer.
predicates.no_escaped_capital_gains_income: No capital-gains income escaped assessment because the consideration received was correctly disclosed and no taxable gain arose under the applicable rule.

issues.definition: A reassessment lacks jurisdiction when it is challenged and the bona fide transfer’s consideration was correctly disclosed, leaving no escaped capital-gains income.
